annotation.title_clean: Rethinking the I-You relation through dialogical philosophy in the Ethics of AI and robotics
annotation.title_en: Rethinking the I-You relation through dialogical philosophy in the Ethics of AI and robotics
annotation.summary_en: Editorial introducing an AI & Society special issue applying Martin Buber's dialogical philosophy (I and Thou) to the ethics of social robots and AI. It questions instrumental conceptions of relationship in relational robotics, raises dehumanisation concerns, and summarises the contributions. It does not propose any governance measures.
key_provisions_or_claims: Relational robotics and AI research rests on an egocentric, instrumental model of relationships.
Buber's I-Thou dialogical philosophy is offered as an ethical counterpoint for robotics.
Contributors disagree on whether an I-Thou relation with an artificial agent is possible.
Dehumanisation narratives should be reclaimed rather than dismissed as Luddism.
Embodied, present human relations should be valued over machine-mediated interaction.
